findings.title: Hardcoded credential

findings.message: Call to dangerous builtin eval() enables arbitrary code execution.
findings.remediation: Avoid eval/exec on untrusted input. Use a dispatch dictionary of callables or ast.literal_eval for safe literal parsing.
findings.title: Arbitrary code execution

findings.message: Dynamically constructed SQL query (f-string). Parameterise the query to prevent injection.
findings.remediation: Use parameterised queries (placeholders) instead of f-strings, string concatenation or .format(). Example: cursor.execute('SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?', (user_id,)).
findings.title: SQL injection via dynamic query

findings.message: Call to render_template_string() with possibly untrusted content may inject HTML/JS into the response.
findings.remediation: Do not return raw HTML built from user input. Rely on the templating engine's contextual auto-escaping (Jinja autoescape, Django's escape filter) and never mark user-controlled strings as 'safe'.
findings.title: Possible Cross-Site Scripting

findings.message: Call to Markup() with possibly untrusted content may inject HTML/JS into the response.
findings.remediation: Do not return raw HTML built from user input. Rely on the templating engine's contextual auto-escaping (Jinja autoescape, Django's escape filter) and never mark user-controlled strings as 'safe'.
findings.title: Possible Cross-Site Scripting

findings.message: Template() constructed from a dynamic string – SSTI risk.
findings.remediation: Never compile a template from user input. Render fixed template files and pass user data only as render context variables. If dynamic content is required, sandbox the environment (jinja2.sandbox.SandboxedEnvironment) and restrict globals.
findings.title: Server-Side Template Injection

findings.message: os.system() invoked with a dynamically built command string – classic command injection sink.
findings.remediation: Pass arguments as a list and keep shell=False (the default). When a shell is unavoidable, sanitize input with shlex.quote() and validate against an allow-list of expected values.
findings.title: OS command injection

findings.message: subprocess call with shell=True executes the command via the shell; combined with user input this enables command injection.
findings.remediation: Pass arguments as a list and keep shell=False (the default). When a shell is unavoidable, sanitize input with shlex.quote() and validate against an allow-list of expected values.
findings.title: OS command injection

findings.message: pickle.loads() deserializes arbitrary data; an attacker-controlled payload can lead to RCE.
findings.remediation: Never deserialize data from untrusted sources with pickle/marshal/shelve. Prefer JSON for data exchange; for YAML always use yaml.safe_load() (never plain yaml.load() without SafeLoader).
findings.title: Insecure deserialization

findings.message: yaml.load() without SafeLoader is unsafe; use yaml.safe_load() instead.
findings.remediation: Never deserialize data from untrusted sources with pickle/marshal/shelve. Prefer JSON for data exchange; for YAML always use yaml.safe_load() (never plain yaml.load() without SafeLoader).
findings.title: Insecure deserialization

findings.message: ElementTree.fromstring() from the stdlib does not protect against XXE; use defusedxml for untrusted XML.
findings.remediation: Replace stdlib XML parsers with the defusedxml package when parsing untrusted input. For lxml, instantiate XMLParser with resolve_entities=False and no_network=True.
findings.title: XML External Entity expansion

findings.message: lxml XMLParser created with resolve_entities=True; external entities will be expanded.
findings.remediation: Replace stdlib XML parsers with the defusedxml package when parsing untrusted input. For lxml, instantiate XMLParser with resolve_entities=False and no_network=True.
findings.title: XML External Entity expansion
